title: Sanzo Wada colour dictionary, indexed for early-1900s heritage workwear styling

book.title: A Dictionary of Color Combinations
book.author: Sanzo Wada (和田三造), 1883-1967
book.contents: 159 named colours, 348 combinations of 2, 3 and 4 colours; colours split across 6 swatch books; CMYK given for each colour.

data_source.name: mattdesl/dictionary-of-colour-combinations
data_source.notes: CMYK from the book; RGB/hex/LAB via a perceptual CMYK conversion in that project. Screen hex values are an approximation of printed ink, not a colorimetric match. Note that the upstream lab (converted from the book CMYK) and the upstream hex do not always agree: mean CIEDE2000 between them is 1.5 and reaches 7.7 for saturated blues and greens that fall outside the sRGB gamut. Hence lab_srgb.

evidence_key.source: Present in the book / upstream dataset.
evidence_key.computed: Deterministic maths over source values (CIE LAB/LCh, CIEDE2000).
evidence_key.interpretation: Judgement added by this build: a heuristic about early-1900s workwear, not a citation. Period dye and cloth names are drawn from general textile history (indigo, madder, logwood-iron black, cutch and walnut browns, iron-buff, weld, undyed cotton duck and wool) and are not tied to a specific documented source. Treat every workwear field as a tunable default, not a fact.

workwear_scoring.formula: fit = family_weight * chroma_weight[tier][chroma_band] * value_weight, then *0.72 if saturated & (pale|light), *1.06 if saturated & (deep|dark), clamped to 1.0

tiers.workable: 0.55 <= fit < 0.80 - fine as ground or secondary
tiers.off-period: fit < 0.35 - not plausible in a 1900s work wardrobe

workwear_scoring.combination_formula: fit = 0.4*min(member fits) + 0.6*mean(member fits), *0.85 if more than one saturated member

band_definitions.hue_family: LCh hue angle bins, with low-chroma warm hues folded into brown and low-chroma yellow-greens folded into olive.

usage.which_lab_to_use: colors[].lab is the source value converted from the book CMYK - use it for anything about the printed ink. colors[].lab_srgb is recomputed from colors[].hex and is what every distance in this file uses (nearest[], combinations[].*delta_e*, workwear_anchors). Match screen and photo colours against lab_srgb so an exact hex scores 0.
usage.nearest_color_from_hex: Convert the query hex to CIE LAB (D65, sRGB), then minimise CIEDE2000 against colors[].lab_srgb. delta_e_2000 < 2 is a visual match, < 5 is a close cousin, > 10 is a different colour.
usage.lch_basis: lch/hue_family/value_band/chroma_band are derived from the source lab, i.e. they classify the ink Wada specified rather than its sRGB approximation.
usage.substitution: colors[].nearest is ordered by CIEDE2000 and excludes self.

matching_rules.statement: Prefer a combination straight from the book. Only synthesise a palette when no combination satisfies the brief.
matching_rules.implementation: Filter combinations[] by workwear.plausible and required hue_families before generating anything new.

matching_rules.statement: At most one colour with chroma_band in {moderate, saturated} per outfit; the rest must be neutral or muted.
matching_rules.implementation: Count members by chroma_band; reject or demote extra chromatic colours to slots with area_share <= 0.04.

matching_rules.statement: Area is inversely proportional to chroma. Ground 55-70% of visible area, secondary 20-30%, accent 3-10%.
matching_rules.implementation: Sum area_share of assigned slots per role and check against these bands.

matching_rules.statement: Two adjacent layers need delta L* >= 12 (or delta E2000 >= 15) to read as separate garments rather than a failed match.
matching_rules.implementation: Compare lab[0] of colours assigned to touching slots (outer/shirt, shirt/trouser).

matching_rules.statement: Keep all neutrals in one temperature. Warm neutrals (lch h 40-100) with warm, cool (h 180-280) with cool. Mixing them reads as accidental.
matching_rules.implementation: Check lch[2] of every colour with chroma_band in {neutral, muted}.

matching_rules.statement: A dark warm brown (role leather) is compatible with any ground and is the safest way to close an awkward pair.
matching_rules.implementation: When a combination fails, add a colour with role leather and fit_score >= 0.7.

matching_rules.statement: A high-contrast pair of one hue family (light + deep, delta L* >= 45) is period-correct because it is how striped drill was woven.
matching_rules.implementation: Allow combinations whose hue_families length is 1 when lightness_range >= 45.

matching_rules.statement: When swapping a colour for availability, replace it with one from nearest[] that shares hue_family and value_band.
matching_rules.implementation: Walk nearest[] and take the first match on both bands; fall back to hue_family only.

matching_rules.statement: Colours with hue_family in {pink, magenta, violet, teal} should never occupy a slot with area_share > 0.06 in a heritage brief.
matching_rules.implementation: Restrict those families to neckwear, hardware and headwear slots.

matching_rules.statement: A three-colour outfit reads best as three distinct value_bands (e.g. deep + mid + light) rather than three hues at the same lightness.
matching_rules.implementation: Prefer combinations with lightness_range >= 30 for size 3.

outfit_templates.label: Two-tone indigo
outfit_templates.note: Dark indigo over faded indigo; needs delta L* >= 15 between the two blues.

outfit_templates.label: Drab ground with one accent
outfit_templates.note: Wada's most transferable move: quiet ground, one small saturated note.

outfit_templates.label: Canvas and leather
outfit_templates.note: Warm neutral field with brass and tan; keep all neutrals on the warm side.

outfit_templates.label: Sunday-best workwear
outfit_templates.note: Tonal, low-chroma, three values of one hue family plus leather.
